title: Root-cause triage of eval drift after config/model deltas + implement automated smoke tests
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Summary: After a recent config roll (kv-cache tuning + new quantized variant rollout) a production incident surfaced where our nightly eval suite showed a 7-12% drop in answer quality for a customer-critical prompt set. This ticket drives the root-cause triage, produces a short postmortem, and implements a small set of automated smoke checks that run in the CI/CD model/config change path so future regressions are caught before rollout.

Goals: (1) Identify whether the regression was primarily from model variant change, runtime kernel selection, or batching/KV cache behavior. (2) Add deterministic, fast smoke tests that target the failing prompt set and key metrics (EM/ROUGE/semantic-sim) and gate model/config rollouts. (3) Update runbooks and alerting to link eval regressions to deployment events.

Scope: Root-cause triage + one-week follow-up action items; introduce ~5 small smoke tests (<=30s each) to run in PR checks for config/model changes; create a playbook entry for post-deploy eval checks. Not in scope: full retraining or large-scale eval platform redesign (separate initiative).
acceptance_criteria: Causal hypothesis for the incident documented in the postmortem with supporting logs/graphs
At least 5 deterministic smoke tests added to the eval-smoke-suite covering the impacted prompt categories
Smoke tests execute under 60s in CI and block merges when metric regression exceeds threshold
Runbook updated with steps to triage eval drops and a template for incident-driven eval additions
One follow-up ticket created for any remaining medium/long-term mitigations (e.g., kernel rollback automation)
technical_notes: Initial triage: diff of model weights shows identical checkpoints — focus shifted to runtime config delta from 2026-01-12 (batching window and KV-cache warmup policy)
Observed behavior: short-context prompts regress more than long-context. Hypothesis: KV-cache warmup + eager batching changed token scheduling, affecting early-token generation heuristics.
Trade-offs: smoke tests will be intentionally small (few prompts) to keep CI latency low; may not capture all edge cases but will catch dominant regressions linked to recent incident.
Implementation detail: leverage existing eval harness (evals/runner) to produce deterministic seeds and use model pinning in test environment to ensure reproducibility.
Fallback policy: if smoke tests are flaky >2x false positives, adjust thresholds or move to gated canary runs in dedicated environment instead of PR blocking.
updates: 2026-01-15 - Ticket created by Anya after on-call summary flagged eval drop correlated with config rollout.
2026-01-18 - Initial data pulled: nightly-evals shows 9.4% drop on prompt set 'customer-faq-v2'; logs attached to PR.
2026-01-22 - Confirmed model checkpoint unchanged; narrowed to runtime config delta (kv-cache warmup change + batching window tweak).
2026-02-01 - Reproduced regression locally with config-2026-01-12; profiling shows higher latency variance and altered token logits in first 6 tokens.
2026-02-10 - Draft smoke tests implemented covering 'short-qa', 'instruction-following', and 'code-completion' categories; running in nightly branch.
2026-02-24 - Design review with PM and SRE: agreed to keep PR gating for config/model changes limited to 60s. Action: reduce test size and add deterministic seeds.
2026-03-02 - QA run: smoke-suite flaked on 1/40 runs (timeout); lowered parallelism to stabilize. Preparing PR to add tests to CI.
2026-03-05 - Merged prototype smoke tests to feature branch; next: add gating and postmortem write-up.

SRE (Dmitri Ivanov): suggested using a separate small dedicated pod for CI evals to avoid noisy neighbor effects in shared test infra
Design (Rina Cho): asked that failing examples surface counterfactuals to aid debugging (input, expected, actual) in CI output
